lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1  Blogging Mastery –  Cheat Sheet Introduction ü A blog used to be an online journal ü It’s now become a system of content creation and engagement ü Blogging previously focused on frequent posting ü Now bloggers focus on quality over quantity ü A writer now writes to target their readers and their needs ü Bloggers used to grow readership through interaction on the blog ü Today they grow in the same way, but in many different places ü Activities now include tagging, sharing, liking etc ü Social media has meant the blurring of lines ü You can blog using social media, or ‘microblogging’ ü Today blogging can be a viable career  Modern Trends in Blogging Some trends in blogging which are expected to continue: ü Post Length o Posts are longer o They delve deeper into topics o Readers expect greater value ü Fewer Blog Comments o There are increasingly fewer comments o Readers are interacting on social media o More bloggers are turning off comment sections ü Graphics o It’s not only about text-based content

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2  o The quality of graphics is improving o Bloggers have access to better software ü Metrics o Metrics used to focus on traffic o Today they also track engagement o Modern bloggers look at how readers interact ü Platforms o Bloggers have always used one-stop platforms like WordPress o Other options have arisen o It’s not a requirement to use a blogging-specific platform  Learning Objectives:  ü Define your target reader ü Write captivating posts ü Share your posts to maximize engagement ü Make money from your blog ü Evolve your blogging practice   Action Steps: 1. What is the typical length of your blog posts?  Do you have any posts in the 900-1000 word range? Use this target number as your new minimum length.  2. What social platforms are you currently using? How are you engaging with your audience about your blog posts on social media?  3. What metrics are you currently using to track the effectiveness of your blog posts?

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3  Module 1 - Define Your Audience ü When a blog was just a ‘weblog’, bloggers wrote for themselves ü It was an online journal and if people read it, it was a bonus ü Today it’s more sophisticated and more focused on the reader ü The foundation of a blog today is to know who your readers are and what they need ü The number one thing you can do to improve your blog is to research your audience  Your Reader Persona ü The best way to understand your reader is to create a persona or profile ü A detailed description of your ideal reader ü Tailor your content to this single person ü You can create separate profiles for different segments of your audience ü Look for trends among your readership ü Try not to nail down everything  Step 1 – Demographics ü Demographics include: o Age o Geographic location o Language o Gender o Income level o Education level

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4  o Religion o Marital status o Occupation o Family composition ü Discover this data by looking at Facebook Insights and other social media metrics ü Look at your Google Analytics for your blog  Step 2 – Explore Psychographics ü Psychographics include: o Personality o Attitudes o Values o Hobbies o Lifestyle o Behavior o Goals o Challenges o Image of self o Pain points  o Needs and desires ü Psychographics are harder to discover than demographics ü The only way to understand is to observe and interact ü Watch how they behave and what they say ü You also need to understand how they buy and use products and services ü Pay attention to how they interact with products ü Ask yourself:

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5  o Why would the reader want to know about your topic? o How knowledgeable are they? o What common questions do they have? ü A better way to get data is by looking at forums or groups ü Do a search in Google or Reddit ü Also look at what topics or subjects are popular ü Conduct a survey with existing subscribers or readers ü Create a short survey with a tool like survey monkey ü Offer an incentive for completing the survey ü Talk to your readers one-on-one to get the deepest understanding  Step 3 – Learn About Your Reader’s Behaviors and Preferences ü Learn about how they read and engage with the content they like ü Consider: o How do they find content? o What content formats do they like? o How do they consume content? o What is their taste in terms of length and depth of content? ü Go back to the forums and look at the content that’s most popular ü See which topics get the most engagement ü Look at other platforms to see which types of content get the most engagement ü Current analytics can show you which pieces of content readers are staying on ü Google's Keyword Planner tool can tell you what questions are being asked ü Follow industry influencers and watch how they interact with their audience

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6  Step 4 – Create Your Target Reader Profile ü Take all of the information you’ve gathered and put it together as a profile of your target reader ü Give each target a name and treat them individually ü Add a picture for an avatar ü Paragraph 1 should be for demographics ü Paragraph 2 should be for psychographics ü Paragraph 3 should be for behaviour     Action Step: 1. Follow the steps in this chapter to draft your reader profile.

PAGE_7:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 7  Module 2 - Create Captivating and Shareable Content  ü Now you have a clear idea of who your target audience is  ü You can start planning what kind of content you will create ü Blogging takes planning ü Bloggers don’t just sit down and crank out a post each day ü They create lists of idea to draw upon when it’s time to write ü They often set aside special times to write  ü They might write a number of posts to have on hand  ü Start by creating a list of topics ü Brainstorm by asking yourself questions: o What do they want to know about? o What specific questions are they asking? o What problems are they facing? o What are possible solutions to these problems? o What things do you know that they don't which could help them? o What is your audience member searching for? o What topics are your audience members talking about? o What kind of content is your audience sharing or commenting on? ü Aim for quantity when you’re brainstorming ü Get down as many ideas as possible ü Then go back and prioritize them ü Keep in mind that not all content will be text-only ü Think about videos, infographics, etc

PAGE_8:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 8  Creating Titles ü Now, take your list and give each a title ü Your title needs to be catchy and clear ü Turn each topic into a working title ü Titles should be specific as well as catchy ü Using numbers in your title makes it clearer to the reader ü Include the format of the content if it’s not text ü Then create sub-headings  ü This will make things more skim-able ü Each section should have a few paragraphs  Other Tips for Titles Consider Keywords ü Use keywords that people might search for ü Put them as close to the beginning as possible  Use Alliteration ü Use the same letters or sounds ü Repeated sounds make the title catchier  Use Strong Language (in Moderation) ü Make bold claims about what the article delivers ü Make sure you deliver and don’t overuse words  Keep Titles Short ü Make them as short as possible without losing impact ü Keep it under 70 characters

PAGE_9:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 9  Show Your Brand Personality ü Choose words, phrases, and grammar that reflect your personality ü Make sure your titles are consistent with your other content  Writing Your Blog Posts Post Length ü Look at your reader profile to determine your post length ü This varies according to topic and audience ü If you have a topic that’s too long, you can break it up ü It it’s too short, you can add to it or make it part of another post ü It doesn’t need to be the same each time ü Aim for some consistency  Write Like a Journalist ü Start with a basic foundation and build upon it ü Start with the conclusion and then fill in the body ü Gain attention and offer a teaser at the start  Break Up Your Text ü Blogs rarely have huge blocks of text ü Text is broken up by: o Short paragraphs o Line breaks o Images o Bulleted lists o Bold and alternative fonts o Blank space

PAGE_10:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 10  Links and Networking ü Wherever appropriate, add links ü Add a link where you cite an article or discuss a blog ü Link to your own content too ü Link when you mention another blogger ü This can have networking advantages ü Let them know you did but don’t push for a reply  Editing Your Work ü Blog are written in a friendly tone ü You can’t let mistakes slide ü Make sure it’s mistake-free and written in the best way possible ü Some easy ways to edit include: o Always read over your work o Read your work aloud o Sleep on it and read it again o Ask a friend to review it   Action Steps: 1. Generate Blog Post Topics  o Step 1: Start by brainstorming topics o Step 2: Prioritize your topics and select 1-2 to work on o Step 3: Turn your topics into catchy titles o Step 4: Create your subtopics to help you organize your blog post 2. Use the tips in this module to draft your blog post in a separate document or notepad (wherever you write your posts). You can also try rewriting a past blog post as a way to test the new strategies in this module.

PAGE_11:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 11  Module 3 – Share Your Posts for Maximum Reach and Engagement ü Your content isn’t much use unless people are reading and engaging with it ü Aim to get your content shared, liked, and commented upon ü Update social media profiles so that they include a link to your blog ü Include a call-to-action telling readers what benefits to expect ü Add a link to a ‘start here’ post  Spread the Word ü Getting
